content: Cobicistat is a potent inhibitor of the enzyme CYP3A4. It is contraindicated for use with drugs that are substrates of CYP3A4 if elevated plasma concentrations of these drugs are associated with serious or life-threatening events. The combination of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF (E/C/F/TAF) can significantly alter the metabolism of various drugs by inhibiting or inducing specific hepatic and intestinal enzymes, leading to increased or decreased drug levels. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for co-administration: 1. Quinine: E/C/F/TAF increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 2. Quizartinib: E/C/F/TAF increases quizartinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce quizartinib to 4 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Interrupt quizartinib during strong inhibitor use and resume the prior dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor. 3. Ranolazine: E/C/F/TAF increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 4. Repaglinide: E/C/F/TAF increases repaglinide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 5. Ribociclib: Ribociclib increases E/C/F/TAF levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 6. Rifaximin: E/C/F/TAF increases rifaximin levels by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Risperidone: E/C/F/TAF increases risperidone levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. A dose reduction of risperidone may be needed. 8. Roflumilast (topical): E/C/F/TAF increases roflumilast levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Ropivacaine: E/C/F/TAF increases ropivacaine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 10. Ruxolitinib: E/C/F/TAF increases ruxolitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 11. Salbutamol: E/C/F/TAF increases salbutamol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 12. Salmeterol: E/C/F/TAF increases salmeterol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 13. Salsalate: Co-administration with E/C/F/TAF may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Monitor closely and consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 14. Saxagliptin: E/C/F/TAF increases saxagliptin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce saxagliptin dose to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 15. Seladelpar: E/C/F/TAF increases seladelpar levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for adverse effects. 16. Selexipag: E/C/F/TAF increases selexipag levels by inhibiting ABCG2 (BCRP). Monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects. 17. Sertraline: E/C/F/TAF increases sertraline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 18. Sirolimus: E/C/F/TAF increases sirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 19. Sofosbuvir: Sofosbuvir increases E/C/F/TAF levels through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Solifenacin: E/C/F/TAF increases solifenacin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 21. Streptomycin: Co-administration with E/C/F/TAF increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Sufentanil: E/C/F/TAF increases sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely to avoid respiratory depression. 23. Sulfadiazine: E/C/F/TAF decreases sulfadiazine levels by inducing CYP2C9. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Sulindac: Co-administration with E/C/F/TAF may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Monitor closely and consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 25. Sunitinib: E/C/F/TAF increases sunitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 26. Tacrolimus: E/C/F/TAF increases tacrolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Tadalafil: E/C/F/TAF increases tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust tadalafil dose for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) or erectile dysfunction (ED) as recommended. 28. Tamoxifen: E/C/F/TAF decreases tamoxifen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6, potentially reducing its conversion to active metabolites. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 29. Tamsulosin: E/C/F/TAF increases tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 30. Temsirolimus: E/C/F/TAF increases temsirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 31. Teniposide: E/C/F/TAF increases teniposide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 32. Terbinafine: E/C/F/TAF increases terbinafine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Tetracycline: E/C/F/TAF increases tetracycline levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 34. Theophylline: E/C/F/TAF increases theophylline levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 35. Thioridazine: E/C/F/TAF increases thioridazine levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. A dose reduction may be needed. 36. Tiagabine: E/C/F/TAF increases tiagabine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 37. Ticlopidine: E/C/F/TAF increases ticlopidine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 38. Timolol: E/C/F/TAF increases timolol levels via CYP2D6 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 39. Tinidazole: E/C/F/TAF increases tinidazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 40. Tisotumab vedotin: E/C/F/TAF increases tisotumab vedotin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. 41. Tobramycin: Co-administration with E/C/F/TAF increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Tolmetin: Co-administration with E/C/F/TAF may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Monitor closely and consider alternatives to NSAIDs. 43. Tolterodine: E/C/F/TAF increases tolterodine levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 44. Toremifene: E/C/F/TAF increases toremifene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 45. Torsemide: E/C/F/TAF decreases torsemide levels by inducing CYP2C9. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Tramadol: E/C/F/TAF increases tramadol levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 47. Trazodone: E/C/F/TAF increases trazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 48. Triamcinolone acetonide (injectable suspension): E/C/F/TAF increases triamcinolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Triazolam: E/C/F/TAF increases triazolam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider reducing the benzodiazepine dose. 50. Trimethoprim: E/C/F/TAF affects trimethoprim levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C9. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Trimipramine: E/C/F/TAF increases trimipramine levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 52. Ublituximab: Ublituximab may reduce the effects of E/C/F/TAF due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Monitor closely. 53. Umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol (inhaled): E/C/F/TAF increases vilanterol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 54. Valacyclovir: Co-administration with E/C/F/TAF may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Monitor closely. 55. Valbenazine: E/C/F/TAF increases valbenazine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce valbenazine dose to 40 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 56. Valganciclovir: Co-administration with E/C/F/TAF may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Monitor closely. 57. Vamorolone: E/C/F/TAF increases vamorolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the starting dose of vamorolone to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients weighing over 50 kg. 58. Vancomycin: Co-administration with E/C/F/TAF increases nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Vardenafil: E/C/F/TAF increases vardenafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 60. Venlafaxine: E/C/F/TAF increases venlafaxine levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 61. Verapamil: E/C/F/TAF increases verapamil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 62. Vilazodone: E/C/F/TAF increases vilazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 63. Vinblastine: E/C/F/TAF increases vinblastine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 64. Vincristine: E/C/F/TAF increases vincristine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 65. Vinorelbine: E/C/F/TAF increases vinorelbine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 66. Voriconazole: Co-administration with E/C/F/TAF may increase levels of both drugs due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Assess the benefit/risk ratio before co-administration. 67. Zafirlukast: E/C/F/TAF decreases zafirlukast levels by inducing CYP2C9. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Zanubrutinib: E/C/F/TAF increases zanubrutinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 69. Zolpidem: E/C/F/TAF increases zolpidem levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 70. Zonisamide: E/C/F/TAF increases zonisamide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. In summary, the combination of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF has significant interactions with numerous drugs, primarily through its inhibition of CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 enzymes. These interactions necessitate careful monitoring, dose adjustments, or avoidance of certain drugs to prevent toxicity or reduced therapeutic efficacy.
